//: module/moduleResolution are NodeNext, not bundler, and that is a
PRODUCTION BUG FIX rather than a preference.
package.json declares "type": "module", so Vercel runs these routes as
real Node ESM. Node ESM does not do extension resolution: an import of
"../_lib/userContext" is a literal file path and there is no file there.
Under "bundler" resolution TypeScript accepted those extensionless
specifiers, typecheck passed, the build passed, and EVERY api/ route then
died at first invocation in production with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND — a
failure no local check could see, because vitest resolves them fine.
NodeNext makes tsc apply Node's own rules, so a missing ".js" extension
is now a typecheck error at the same moment it is written.
